extracted.intended_audience: public relations / crisis communications teams and communications professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and a checklist for drafting crisis press releases that acknowledge incidents, apologize when appropriate, communicate facts and actions, and maintain appropriate tone and channels. Emphasizes structure, timing, and responsibility-based responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline
rubrics_metrics.description: The release headline should directly address the situation and name the issue clearly without spin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not be defensive or evasive; avoid spin. Make the headline directly address the situation and state the issue clearly so audiences immediately understand the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: First paragraph must acknowledge what happened and express appropriate concern for those affected using plain facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't bury the news; open with a plain statement of facts and clearly acknowledge the incident and concern for affected parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body content (details and response)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed information about the incident and what the organization is doing in response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include organization's actions taken, a statement from a high-ranking official, an expression of concern plus commitment to resolution, resources for affected parties, a timeline of events, and an update plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to apologize
rubrics_metrics.description: Apologize when the organization is clearly at fault or actions/negligence have harmed people; an authentic apology is essential to rebuild trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only apologize when fault is clear or harm occurred; an authentic apology is necessary for trust restoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to apologize
rubrics_metrics.description: Apology should be sincere, humble, and show competence — no excuses — and should be placed at the front of the crisis statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a humble but competent tone; no-excuses sincerity; ensure audiences know you're sorry and able to enact solutions; apology should appear FIRST in any crisis statement; show affected people are foremost in your thoughts; demonstrate understanding of severity and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and approach — Do
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred tonal and behavioral practices in crisis statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show cooperation and accountability; express empathy; be transparent about known facts; acknowledge unknowns; outline corrective actions; provide regular updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and approach — Don't
rubrics_metrics.description: Behaviors and language to avoid in crisis statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make excuses, deflect blame, minimize impact, use jargon or legalese, speculate, promise what you can't deliver, or use passive voice (e.g., 'mistakes were made').

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard crisis release structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended element order and components for a crisis press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: 1) Acknowledgment (what happened, when); 2) Empathy (concern for affected parties); 3) Apology (if at fault) — sincere & specific; 4) Facts (what we know); 5) Action (what we're doing); 6) Support (resources for affected); 7) Accountability (who is responsible); 8) Update plan (when more info is coming); 9) Contact (for more information).

rubrics_metrics.name: Match response to crisis responsibility (High responsibility / Preventable)
rubrics_metrics.description: For preventable crises where organization has high responsibility: lead with apology and corrective measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apology plus corrective action; offer compensation where appropriate; use mortification strategy (full apology/acceptance of responsibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Match response to crisis responsibility (Medium responsibility / Accidental)
rubrics_metrics.description: For accidental crises where responsibility is partial or ambiguous: acknowledge and explain, and commit to corrective action and empathy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide acknowledgment and explanation, outline corrective actions, and express empathy for those affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match response to crisis responsibility (Low responsibility / Victim)
rubrics_metrics.description: For crises where the organization is a victim or has low responsibility: focus on response information and support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide information about your response, express empathy, and offer resources for affected parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge within 24 hours
rubrics_metrics.description: A crisis should be publicly acknowledged within 24 hours of discovery or when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely acknowledgment is required to maintain credibility; this is listed as an explicit implicit standard: 'Acknowledged within 24 hours.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge incident clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: The release must clearly state and acknowledge the incident rather than obfuscate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain language, do not bury or obscure the incident; make the acknowledgement explicit and unambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express empathy
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate empathy and concern for those affected as an explicit component of the message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show sincere concern and empathy; make affected people the focus of the message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apologize if at fault (specific apology)
rubrics_metrics.description: When at fault, provide a specific and sincere apology rather than a vague or conditional statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apology should be explicit ('we are sorry'), specific about what you're apologizing for, and free of excuses or conditional language.

rubrics_metrics.name: State facts known
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly state the facts that are known about the incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide verifiable details and the timeline of events; be transparent about what has been confirmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note facts unknown
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge what is not yet known about the incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state uncertainties and what is being investigated; avoid speculation but acknowledge gaps in knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outline actions taken
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe concrete actions the organization has taken in response to the incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List immediate remediation, safety measures, investigations launched, corrective actions, and timelines for those actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide resources for affected
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer support resources and guidance for those impacted by the incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include hotlines, online resources, support centers, compensation information where applicable, and how to access assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name accountable party
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify who within the organization is accountable for the incident or for leading the response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the responsible team or individual and how accountability will be enforced or examined; avoid vague or diffuse responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide update timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: State when the public can expect further information or updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give a clear update plan with dates/times or conditions that will trigger the next update; promise only what you can deliver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct contact for media
rubrics_metrics.description: Include direct media contact information for follow-up questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide phone, email, and hours available; designate a single spokesperson to handle media inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designate a single spokesperson
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign one spokesperson to ensure consistent public communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single, trained spokesperson prevents mixed messages; provide their contact and availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate across channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the message is consistent and coordinated across all communication channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align press release, social media, website statements, and internal communications; maintain consistency in facts, tone, and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use plain language (no spin)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid spin, jargon, or legalese — communicate plainly and clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use straightforward language accessible to general audiences; avoid euphemisms and corporate-speak that minimize the impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid defensive posture
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not take a defensive or evasive tone in the crisis statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid deflecting blame, making excuses, or minimizing harm; be accountable and empathetic instead.
